content: 1. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 2. Fosaprepitant decreases the levels or effects of ubrogepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Dose adjustments are necessary when ubrogepant is used with moderate or weak CYP3A4 inducers. 3. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Vardenafil dosage may need to be reduced when co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 4. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor closely for signs of venetoclax toxicities. 5. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 6. Fosaprepitant increases the levels of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If intolerable adverse effects occur, reduce the daily dose of vilazodone to 20 mg. 7. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 8. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of vincristine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 9. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of liposomal vincristine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 10. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 11. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Fosaprepitant decreases the levels or effects of warfarin by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. In patients on chronic warfarin therapy, monitor INR during the two-week period following fosaprepitant administration, particularly at 7–10 days after each chemotherapy cycle. 14. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 16. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Interrupt dosing as recommended for adverse reactions. Resume the previous dose of zanubrutinib after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 17. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 18. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 19. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 20. Adverse effects associated with fosaprepitant include leukopenia (2%), dyspepsia (2%), urinary tract infections (2%), and extremity pain (2%). Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders such as pruritus, rash, urticaria, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported. Immune system disorders include hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and anaphylactic shock. Nervous system disorders such as ifosfamide-induced neurotoxicity have been reported when fosaprepitant is co-administered with ifosfamide. 21. Data on the use of fosaprepitant in pregnant females are insufficient to determine drug-associated risks. It is unknown if the drug is excreted in human milk. Decisions regarding discontinuation of nursing or the drug should consider the importance of the drug to the mother. 22. Fosaprepitant is generally acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. 23. For intravenous administration of fosaprepitant: Patients aged >17 years: Infuse over 20–30 minutes. Patients aged 12–17 years: Infuse over 30 minutes. Patients aged 6 months to <12 years: Infuse over 60 minutes. 24. The above information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only.
